value.0: Apex Bite. Closed the file. You put six tallies of trouble in the ground and the preserve's mine again on paper and in fact. Don't come back looking for more of it; there isn't any.

Pens are wrong again. Feed's wrong. And now you, standing in my gate like you've got nothing better to do. You're not ready for what's living past that fence. Come back once you've actually got a handle on that beast of yours, not before.

Pen count's six short and I know exactly who took them. Adepts, they call themselves, keeper crew that moved in on my preserve like it was theirs to feed. Go into the Tarn Jungle Preserve on Dathomir. Put down six of them. Bring me the Apex Bite Tarn Hunt Tally off whichever one's still holding it. I need my numbers back before the surveyors come asking.
Key's yours. Gate's on the north fence line, the one with the busted latch I never got around to fixing. Go in, get my count, get out. I don't pay for sightseeing.

Keeper crew, self-appointed. Feed the beasts on fear instead of feed, if you want my honest opinion. A scared animal bites first and asks never. Good for a killing floor. Terrible for a preserve I'm supposed to hand back in one piece.

One bite. Committed, no second try, no half-measures. That's the whole technique, done right. These adepts try it scared and rushed, which just means a lot of animals get hurt for nothing. Waste of good teeth.

Because when the surveyors finally show up to audit this place, they want numbers that add up. Six missing tallies is six questions I don't have good answers for. Bring it back and I've got one less hole in my paperwork and one less reason to lose this preserve for good.
Six adepts still walking around with my tally. Go finish the count.
You're still standing, which is more than I expected honestly. Hand it over.
Numbers match again. That's one problem off my desk. There's more of them in there if you're not done making yourself useful.

Five specialists running the pens now, mixing scent into the feed to keep the animals angry around the clock. Bad for the beasts, worse for anyone who has to walk past those pens after. Go back in, put the five down, bring me the Apex Bite Beast-Pen Scent Vial they're using.
Same fence, same busted latch. Deeper in, though. Watch your footing near the pens; the ground gets soft where they've been dumping runoff.

Preserve scent-vials are supposed to calm a spooked animal, mark it as safe ground. Theirs does the opposite on purpose. Bring it back and I can prove what they've been feeding my beasts, which is exactly the kind of proof an audit wants.

An angry animal is a predictable animal, in a bad way. Charges the first thing that moves. Doesn't think, doesn't wait, doesn't choose. Easier to point at a target when there's nothing left in it but rage. Cruelty dressed up as training.

You don't. A furious animal swings wild and hopes. A true apex bite waits for the one committed opening and takes it clean. Rage burns hot and sloppy. Discipline waits and lands once. That's the whole difference, and it's the whole reason my preserve trained it right in the first place.
Five specialists still poisoning my feed lines. Bring that vial back.
You smell like the pens. Hopefully in the good way. Let's see it.
That's evidence, that is. Whatever audit finally shows up, this makes my case for me. Good work.

There's a warden holding the deep bay, the one who trained the specialists to poison a feed line in the first place. Committed bite, same as the rest of them, except his lands and nobody's ever walked away from it solo. My rule's posted at every gate for a reason: no solo entry on anything past the third fence. Bring two more with you. Put him down. Bring me the Apex Bite Clawed Alpha Totem he's carrying.
Same latch. Deep bay's past the drainage ditch, watch the footing. Bring your two in with you, not behind you. I've had reports go quiet on that difference before.

Ran my breeding program once, before the keeper crew showed up and made him a better offer. Knows every animal in that bay by name still, which is exactly why he's dangerous. He's not guessing where the apex bite lands. He's certain.

Alpha totem's supposed to mark the top of a healthy line, the animal every other one in the pen learns from. He's carrying it cracked because he cracked the line itself the day he switched sides. Whole totem back in my hands, and I've got proof of exactly which line got corrupted and when.

Because I've buried the paperwork on every keeper who thought they could handle the deep bay alone. One bite lands, that's the whole fight, over, before you've even registered what happened. Three sets of eyes watching three directions means somebody sees it coming. One set of eyes just means one funeral.
The deep bay's still his. Get your two and finish it.
All three of you upright, which tells me you actually listened to the rule for once. Let's see the totem.

Whole. That's the breeding line back under honest management, at least on paper. I'll be filing this one myself. Rest up. The inner circle's next, and they won't like what just happened to their warden.

Four keepers left running this whole operation, the inner circle, the ones who wrote the feed schedules that poisoned my pens in the first place. Bring your two back. Four of them together means four directions of trouble at once. Put them down. Bring me the Apex Bite Preserve Keeper's Token they hold between them.
Same fence. Deepest part of the preserve, where the old records office used to be before they gutted it. Stay close to your two. Four keepers coordinate. You'd better too.

The whole operation. Feed schedules, pen assignments, which animal gets which handler. Everything I used to run honestly, they run for profit and cruelty in equal measure. Cut off the head and the rest of this mess falls apart fast.

That token's the closest thing this preserve has to a deed. Whoever holds it can sign off on feed orders, pen transfers, all of it. They minted their own copies to make it look legal. One real token in my hand, and every signature they've made since gets thrown out.

Same way any bad operation runs smooth for a while: divide the work, keep everyone too busy to ask questions. One handles feed, one handles pens, one handles intake, one handles whoever asks too many questions. That's you now, apparently.
Four keepers, still running my records office like it's theirs. Bring the token back.
Still three of you. Good. Let's see what they were holding.
That's the deed back where it belongs. One name left on this whole operation, and it's the one who built it. You've earned the last entry in this file.

Last name in the file: the master. Built this whole operation out of an apex bite done right, then decided right meant landing it on anything that questioned him. He doesn't miss and he doesn't need a second try, same discipline I trained into this preserve in the first place, aimed at the wrong things for years now. Bring your two. No solo entry, not for this, not for anyone. There's no token this time. Him going down is the whole audit, closed for good.
Then go. Same fence, same latch, all the way to the old main lodge. Stay together. I don't want to be filing three separate reports instead of one good one.

Everyone else's bite is a strike. His is a certainty. He's never once landed it wrong in all the years I've watched this preserve go bad, and that's not luck, that's the technique done exactly as it's meant to be done, aimed at people instead of prey. That's what you've been learning to do right this whole time. He's just been doing it wrong, expertly.

Because one committed bite only needs one opening, and against three of you spread out, he doesn't get to choose which opening he wants. He gets whatever's left. That's the whole math of it. Against one target, he chooses. Against three, he's chosen for.

Goes back to being a preserve instead of a killing floor with a feed schedule. I'll have the pens right again inside a season, if the surveyors don't beat me to shutting the whole place down out of spite. Either way, that's my problem, not yours. Yours is finishing this.
He's still in the old lodge. Bring your two, and finish the file.
Quiet out past the fence. Preserve hasn't been that quiet since before all this started. Tell me it's him.

Then the file's closed. Pens are mine again, on paper and in fact, and the surveyors can find some other preserve to worry about. You did what I trained this place to do in the first place, done right, one committed strike at a time. Go feed that beast of yours something decent for once.
Back to the count.
I'll settle your tally and bring it back.
Who took over your pens?
What's an apex bite, exactly?
Why does this tally matter so much?
Not my problem yet.
Here's the Apex Bite Tarn Hunt Tally.
Back to the count.
I'll shut down the five and bring the vial.
What's in the vial they're using?
Why keep the beasts angry on purpose?
How do you land a bite on something that's already furious?
Give me a day to think about it.
Here's the Apex Bite Beast-Pen Scent Vial.
Back to the count.
I'll get two more and take the deep bay.
Who is this warden to your preserve?
What's the alpha totem, and why's the audit care?
Why exactly is solo entry against the rules?
Haven't got my two yet.
Here's the Apex Bite Clawed Alpha Totem, whole.
Back to the count.
We'll take the four of them together.
What does the inner circle actually run?
What's this keeper's token worth to your audit?
How do four keepers manage a whole preserve like this?
My two need a rest first.
Here's the Apex Bite Preserve Keeper's Token, whole.
Back to the count.
We're going in for him, together.
How is his bite different from everyone else's?
Why does it take three of us for one committed strike?
What happens to the preserve, once he's gone?
Not till we're all ready.
It's done. He's down.
